name: ropivacaine
notes: Long-acting amide LA; the pure S-enantiomer, markedly LESS cardiotoxic than racemic bupivacaine at similar CNS potency (the agent-choice safety argument — v0.6 LA2). Highly bound (~94%). Lower lipid solubility and slightly higher clearance than bupivacaine. Concentrations in ug/mL.

protein_binding.note: ~94% bound, principally to α1-acid glycoprotein. As with bupivacaine the binding saturates; the LA-specific free-fraction story is v0.6 LA1/LA3, distinct from the v0.5 albumin axis (binding_sensitive=false).

cardiotoxicity_class.mechanism: Pure S-enantiomer with lower lipophilicity and less avid cardiac Na-channel binding than racemic bupivacaine — markedly less cardiotoxic at similar local-anesthetic potency. The cardiovascular margin over the CNS-warning range is wider, so CNS symptoms more reliably precede cardiovascular toxicity.
cardiotoxicity_class.note: The agent-choice safety argument (v0.6 LA2): for the same block, ropivacaine's wider CNS-to-CVS margin is the reason it (and levobupivacaine) displaced racemic bupivacaine where cardiotoxicity risk dominates.
